[MATH: \iiint\limits_R f(x,y,z) \:\textrm{d}V = \int_0^1\int_{\sqrt{z}}^1\int_0^{y^2-z} f(x,y,z) \:\textrm{d}x\:\textrm{d}y\:\textrm{d}z]

sections.normalized_html:
From the given repeated integral, we see that [MATH: R] can be written as a type II region as follows:

[MATH: R = \big\{ (x,y,z) \: : \: 0 \leq z \leq 1, \:\: \sqrt{z} \leq y \leq 1, \:\: 0 \leq x \leq y^2-z \big\}]

We wish to rewrite our triple integral as follows:

[MATH: \iiint\limits_R f(x,y,z) \:\textrm{d}V = \int_a^b\int_{v_1(y)}^{v_2(y)}\int_{u_1(y,z)}^{u_2(y,z)} f(x,y,z) \:\textrm{d}x\:\textrm{d}z\:\textrm{d}y]

Since both repeated integrals first integrate with respect to [MATH: x,] the [MATH: x]-limits remain the same as before:

[MATH: \iiint\limits_R f(x,y,z) \:\textrm{d}V = \int_a^b\int_{v_1(y)}^{v_2(y)}\int_0^{y^2-z} f(x,y,z) \:\textrm{d}x\:\textrm{d}z\:\textrm{d}y]

Now, we consider the projection [MATH: D] of [MATH: R] onto the [MATH: yz]-plane shown below.

The region [MATH: D] is a type II region in the [MATH: yz]-plane:

[MATH: D = \big\{ (y,z) \: : \: 0 \leq z \leq 1, \:\: \sqrt{z} \leq y \leq 1 \big\}]

To change the order of integration from [MATH: \textrm{d}x\:\textrm{d}y\:\textrm{d}z] to [MATH: \textrm{d}x\:\textrm{d}z\:\textrm{d}y,] we write [MATH: D] as a type I region.

Notice that the top boundary of the region, written in the form [MATH: z=z(y),] is

[MATH: y=\sqrt{z} \qquad\Longrightarrow\qquad z = y^2]

and the bottom boundary of the region is

[MATH: z=0.]

Then, the type I representation of the region [MATH: D] is

[MATH: D = \big\{ (y,z) \: : \: 0 \leq y \leq 1, \:\: 0 \leq z\leq y^2 \big\},]

as shown below.

Therefore, by swapping the order of integration, we obtain [MATH: \iiint\limits_R f(x,y,z) \:\textrm{d}V = \int_0^1 \int_{0}^{y^2} \int_0^{y^2-z} f(x,y,z) \:\textrm{d}x\:\textrm{d}z\:\textrm{d}y.]

Item 1 — Tutorial: Introduction

Content:
Suppose we want to evaluate the following repeated integral:
[MATH: \int_0^1\int_{x^2}^{1} \int_{0}^{1}\,\dfrac{e^{y}}{\sqrt{y}}\,\textrm{d}z\, \textrm{d}y\, \textrm{d}x]

Content:
For this repeated integral, the integration domain is the type I region

Content:
[MATH: R = \big\{ (x,y,z) \: : \: 0 \leq x \leq 1, \:\: x^2 \leq y \leq 1, \:\: 0 \leq z \leq 1 \big\}]

Content:
as illustrated below.

Graphic:
[IMG: /graphics/c312b162fe8679854854d4e56e44db97]

Content:
The expression '[MATH: \,\textrm{d}z\, \textrm{d}y\, \textrm{d}x]' means we should integrate first with respect to [MATH: z,] then with respect to [MATH: y,] and lastly with respect to [MATH: x.] Let's see what happens when we attempt to integrate in this order:

Content:
[MATH: ∫_{0}^{1}∫_{x^{2}}^{1}∫_{0}^{1}(e^{y})/(sqrt(y))dzdydx|= ∫_{0}^{1}∫_{x^{2}}^{1}(e^{y})/(sqrt(y))[∫_{0}^{1}dz]dydx; = ∫_{0}^{1}∫_{x^{2}}^{1}(e^{y})/(sqrt(y)) ⋅ [z]_{0}^{1}dydx; = ∫_{0}^{1}∫_{x^{2}}^{1}(e^{y})/(sqrt(y))dydx]

Content:
Notice that we cannot proceed any further because we cannot find a simple antiderivative of [MATH: \dfrac{e^{y}}{\sqrt{y}}.]

Content:
To resolve this issue, we first note that the projection of [MATH: R] onto the [MATH: xy]-plane is the type I plane region [MATH: D] shown below.

Graphic:
[IMG: /graphics/1cfbc149f6a15bc901cfef827a473653]

Content:
This region can also be represented as the type II plane region.

Graphic:
[IMG: /graphics/8ee1d129ca5280cc25540b7c872a3e3d]

Content:
Using set notation, [MATH: D]'s representation as a type II plane region is
[MATH: D = \big\{ (x,y) \: : \: 0 \leq y \leq 1, \:\: 0 \leq x \leq \sqrt{y} \big\}.]

Content:
Therefore, we can evaluate this integral by keeping the inner integral the same and swapping the order of integration in the middle and outer integrals:

Content:
[MATH: ∫_{0}^{1}∫_{x^{2}}^{1}∫_{0}^{1}(e^{y})/(sqrt(y))dzdydx|= ∫_{0}^{1}∫_{0}^{sqrt(y)}∫_{0}^{1}(e^{y})/(sqrt(y))dzdxdy]

Content:
Now, we evaluate this integral.

Content:
[MATH: ∫_{0}^{1}∫_{0}^{sqrt(y)}∫_{0}^{1}(e^{y})/(sqrt(y))dzdxdy|= ∫_{0}^{1}∫_{0}^{sqrt(y)}(e^{y})/(sqrt(y))[∫_{0}^{1}dz]dxdy; = ∫_{0}^{1}∫_{0}^{sqrt(y)}(e^{y})/(sqrt(y))[z]_{0}^{1}dxdy; = ∫_{0}^{1}∫_{0}^{sqrt(y)}(e^{y})/(sqrt(y))dxdy; = ∫_{0}^{1}(e^{y})/(sqrt(y))[∫_{0}^{sqrt(y)}dx]dy; = ∫_{0}^{1}(e^{y})/(sqrt(y)) ⋅ [x]_{0}^{sqrt(y)}dy; = ∫_{0}^{1}(e^{y})/(sqrt(y)) ⋅ sqrt(y)dy; = ∫_{0}^{1}e^{y}dy; = e^{y}|_{0}^{1}; = e − 1]

Content:
Note the following:

Content:
- In this lesson, we'll learn how to compute triple integrals by changing the representation of the projection [MATH: D] of [MATH: R] from a type I plane region to type II (and vice-versa).
- It's also possible to change the spatial (i.e., three-dimensional) representation of [MATH: R] from type I to type II, type I to type III, type II to type III, etc. This is slightly more involved, so we'll leave that discussion for a separate lesson.

Content:

%\int_0^1\int_0^1\int_{{x}}^{1} \,6z e^{zy^2}\,\textrm{d}y\, \textrm{d}x\, \, \textrm{d}z &= \int_0^1\int_0^1\int_{{0}}^{y} \,6z e^{zy^2}\,\textrm{d}x\, \textrm{d}y\, \, \textrm{d}z\

Item 2 — Example: Swapping the Order of Integration by Changing the Projection Type

Example Prompt:
[IMG: /graphics/d9125842cf8cd48196ce9ab2ae311a32]

The triple integral of [MATH: f(x,y,z)] over the region [MATH: R] (shown above) can be expressed as the following repeated integral:

[MATH: \iiint\limits_R f(x,y,z) \:\textrm{d}V
=
\int_0^1\int_{\sqrt{z}}^1\int_0^{y^2-z} f(x,y,z) \:\textrm{d}x\:\textrm{d}y\:\textrm{d}z]

Rewrite this repeated integral by integrating first with respect to [MATH: x,] then [MATH: z,] and then [MATH: y.]

Content:
EXPLANATION

Explanation:
From the given repeated integral, we see that [MATH: R] can be written as a type II region as follows:

[MATH: R = \big\{ (x,y,z) \: : \: 0 \leq z \leq 1, \:\: \sqrt{z} \leq y \leq 1, \:\: 0 \leq x \leq y^2-z \big\}]

We wish to rewrite our triple integral as follows:

[MATH: \iiint\limits_R f(x,y,z) \:\textrm{d}V
=
\int_a^b\int_{v_1(y)}^{v_2(y)}\int_{u_1(y,z)}^{u_2(y,z)} f(x,y,z) \:\textrm{d}x\:\textrm{d}z\:\textrm{d}y]

Since both repeated integrals first integrate with respect to [MATH: x,] the [MATH: x]-limits remain the same as before:

[MATH: \iiint\limits_R f(x,y,z) \:\textrm{d}V
=
\int_a^b\int_{v_1(y)}^{v_2(y)}\int_0^{y^2-z} f(x,y,z) \:\textrm{d}x\:\textrm{d}z\:\textrm{d}y]

Now, we consider the projection [MATH: D] of [MATH: R] onto the [MATH: yz]-plane shown below.

[IMG: /graphics/1de21d0b8286065d87483c152533f036]

The region [MATH: D] is a type II region in the [MATH: yz]-plane:

[MATH: D = \big\{ (y,z) \: : \: 0 \leq z \leq 1, \:\: \sqrt{z} \leq y \leq 1 \big\}]

To change the order of integration from [MATH: \textrm{d}x\:\textrm{d}y\:\textrm{d}z] to [MATH: \textrm{d}x\:\textrm{d}z\:\textrm{d}y,] we write [MATH: D] as a type I region.

Notice that the top boundary of the region, written in the form [MATH: z=z(y),] is

[MATH: y=\sqrt{z}
\qquad\Longrightarrow\qquad
z = y^2]

and the bottom boundary of the region is

[MATH: z=0.]

Then, the type I representation of the region [MATH: D] is

[MATH: D = \big\{ (y,z) \: : \: 0 \leq y \leq 1, \:\: 0 \leq z\leq y^2 \big\},]

as shown below.

[IMG: /graphics/a9c473cff1bba6666cf90eca138e4e13]

Therefore, by swapping the order of integration, we obtain
[MATH: \iiint\limits_R f(x,y,z) \:\textrm{d}V
=

\int_0^1 \int_{0}^{y^2} \int_0^{y^2-z} f(x,y,z) \:\textrm{d}x\:\textrm{d}z\:\textrm{d}y.]

Item 5 — Example: Swapping the Order of Integration When the Projection Is Partitioned

Example Prompt:
By changing the order of integration in the following repeated integrals so that they are integrated first with respect to [MATH: z,] then [MATH: y,] and then [MATH: x,] express the following sum as a single repeated integral.

[MATH: \displaystyle
\int_{-1}^0 \int_{y^2}^{1} \int_{x-1}^{y^2} f(x,y,z) \:\textrm{d}z\:\textrm{d}x\:\textrm{d}y
+
\int_0^1 \int_{y}^{1} \int_{x-1}^{y^2} f(x,y,z) \:\textrm{d}z\:\textrm{d}x\:\textrm{d}y]

Content:
EXPLANATION

Explanation:
We wish to find the limits of integration such that our integral can be expressed as
[MATH: \int_a^b \int_{v_1(x)}^{v_2(x)} \int_{u_1(x,y)}^{u_2(x,y)} f(x,y,z) \:\textrm{d}z\:\textrm{d}y\:\textrm{d}x.]

From the repeated integrals, we see that the domain of integration [MATH: R = R_1\cup R_2,] where [MATH: R_1] and [MATH: R_2] are type I regions, is given by

[MATH: R_{1}|= {(x, y, z): − 1 ≤ y ≤ 0, y^{2} ≤ x ≤ 1, x − 1 ≤ z ≤ y^{2}},; R_{2}|= {(x, y, z): 0 ≤ y ≤ 1, y ≤ x ≤ 1, x − 1 ≤ z ≤ y^{2}}.]

Since all repeated integrals first integrate with respect to [MATH: z,] the [MATH: z]-limits remain the same as before:

[MATH: \int_a^b \int_{v_1(x)}^{v_2(x)} \int_{x-1}^{y^2} f(x,y,z) \:\textrm{d}z\:\textrm{d}y\:\textrm{d}x]

Now, we consider the projection [MATH: D] of [MATH: R] onto the [MATH: xy]-plane shown below.

[IMG: /graphics/8a2a53019675f847983cf091720b77e6]

The region [MATH: D] consists of two type II regions in the [MATH: xy]-plane:

[MATH: D =
\left\{ (x,y) \: : \: -1 \leq y \leq 0, \quad y^2 \leq x \leq 1 \right\}
\:\cup\:
\left\{ (x,y) \: : \: 0 \leq y \leq 1, \quad y \leq x \leq 1 \right\}]

To change the order of integration from [MATH: \textrm{d}z\:\textrm{d}x\:\textrm{d}y] to [MATH: \textrm{d}z\:\textrm{d}y\:\textrm{d}x,] we write [MATH: D] as a type I region.

Notice that the lower boundary of the region, written in the form [MATH: y=y(x),] is
[MATH: x=y^2
\qquad\Longrightarrow\qquad
y = -\sqrt{x}]
and the upper boundary of the region is
[MATH: x=y
\qquad\Longrightarrow\qquad
y =x.]

Then, the type I representation of the region is

[MATH: D = \left\{ (x,y) \: : \: 0 \leq x \leq 1, \quad -\sqrt{x} \leq y \leq x \right\},]

as shown in the diagram below.

[IMG: /graphics/2a5803a3e93d07a1a44e35de17918573]

Therefore, by swapping the order of integration, we obtain

[MATH: \int_0^{\bbox[2pt,Gainsboro]{1}} \int_{\bbox[2pt,Gainsboro]{-\sqrt{x}}}^{\bbox[2pt,Gainsboro]{x}} \int_{x-1}^{y^2} f(x,y,z) \:\textrm{d}z\:\textrm{d}y\:\textrm{d}x.]

Item 8 — Example: Evaluating Triple Integrals by Changing the Projection Type

Example Prompt:
Evaluate
[MATH: \displaystyle
\int_{0}^{1} \int_{y}^{1} \int_{0}^{y} 3e^{x^3} \: \textrm{d}z \: \textrm{d}x \: \textrm{d}y.]

Hint: Change change the order of integration to [MATH: \textrm{d}z \: \textrm{d}y \: \textrm{d}x.]

Content:
EXPLANATION

Explanation:
We wish to find the limits of integration such that our integral can be expressed as
[MATH: \int_{a}^{b} \int_{v_1(x)}^{v_2(x)} \int_{u_1(x,y)}^{u_2(x,y)} 3e^{x^3} \:\textrm{d}z \: \textrm{d}y \: \textrm{d}x.]

From the repeated integral, we see that the domain of integration [MATH: R] can be written as a type I region as follows:
[MATH: R = \left\{ (x,y,z) \: : \: 0 \leq y \leq 1, \:\: y \leq x \leq 1, \:\: 0 \leq z \leq y \right\}]

Since all repeated integrals first integrate with respect to [MATH: z,] the [MATH: z]-limits remain the same as before:
[MATH: \int_{a}^{b} \int_{v_1(x)}^{v_2(x)} \int_{0}^{y} 3e^{x^3} \:\textrm{d}z \: \textrm{d}y \: \textrm{d}x]

Now, we consider the projection [MATH: D] of [MATH: R] onto the [MATH: xy]-plane shown below.

[IMG: /graphics/bb0a1978ac6000ee6b166d46b4d5a7b0]

The region [MATH: D] is type II region in the [MATH: xy]-plane:
[MATH: D = \left\{ (x,y) \::\: 0 \leq y \leq 1, \quad y \leq x \leq 1 \right\}]

To change the order of integration from [MATH: \textrm{d}z \: \textrm{d}x \: \textrm{d}y] to [MATH: \textrm{d}z \: \textrm{d}y \: \textrm{d}x,] we write [MATH: D] as a type I region.

Notice that the top boundary of the region, written in the form [MATH: y = y(x),] is
[MATH: x = y \qquad\Longrightarrow \qquad y = x]

and the bottom boundary of the region [MATH: D] is
[MATH: y = 0.]

Then, the type I representation of the region is
[MATH: D = \left\{ (x,y) \::\: 0 \leq x \leq 1, \quad 0 \leq y \leq x \right\},]

as shown in the diagram below.

[IMG: /graphics/9e35eedb89fe4cd2e1aca34b540f9d85]

Therefore, by swapping the order of integration, we obtain

[MATH: ∫_{0}^{1}∫_{y}^{1}∫_{0}^{y}3e^{x^{3}}dzdxdy|= ∫_{0}^{1}∫_{0}^{x}∫_{0}^{y}3e^{x^{3}}dzdydx; = ∫_{0}^{1}∫_{0}^{x}3e^{x^{3}}[∫_{0}^{y}dz]dydx; = ∫_{0}^{1}∫_{0}^{x}3e^{x^{3}}[z]_{0}^{y}dydx; = ∫_{0}^{1}∫_{0}^{x}3ye^{x^{3}}dydx; = ∫_{0}^{1}3e^{x^{3}}[∫_{0}^{x}ydy]dx; = ∫_{0}^{1}3e^{x^{3}}[(1)/(2)y^{2}]_{0}^{x}dx; = ∫_{0}^{1}(3)/(2)x^{2}e^{x^{3}}dx; = (1)/(2)[e^{x^{3}}]_{0}^{1}; = (1)/(2)(e − 1).]
